items.title: Release target and D12 build/restore plan, including removal granularity
items.target: ingest/DECISIONS.md (owner) and docs/releases/<ver>-sources.json; one D12 build per batch (or per 'build' label)
items.size: policy text and release notes only
user_decision_needed: target release for the absorbed batches: the untagged 2.0.0 PR (oaw-ref/VERSION.json release_status 'proposed', no tag published) or later releases. Compatibility table (revision 3, goldfish-2 B08). Incompatible default behaviour under SemVer 2.0: OAW-19 (search with no match on a non-empty knowledge base 0 -> 4; get on a missing topic 1 -> 4, context_hub.py:244-245; an ambiguous get 3), OAW-12 and OAW-13 (memory add and annotate refuse credential-shaped text, balanced <private> blocks and host wrapper tags that are accepted today), OAW-25 (a doctor FAIL turns a project with a shadowing scripts/ module 'unhealthy', oaw.py:713). Strict mode only: OAW-14, OAW-21 and OAW-23 add lint findings that are warnings by default and, like every soft warning, errors under lint --strict (wiki_sync.py:848-849), so a --strict run that passes today can fail. Default output: OAW-23 adds one renderer_version frontmatter line per compiled page (a one-time diff at the next build); OAW-16 adds one notice line to every recall output only if its A/B passes. Additive: new flags, commands and default-mode warnings (OAW-11, OAW-15, OAW-17, OAW-18, OAW-20, OAW-22, OAW-24). Recommended: every batch into the untagged 2.0.0 while that PR is open (one major version carries every behaviour change, each listed in UPGRADING); after 2.0.0 is tagged, additive items go to 2.x and the incompatible ones wait for 3.0.0

removal granularity (D6, D12). Facts (revision 3, goldfish-1 #13, goldfish-2 B07): restoring build N is linear and also drops every later build; removing one item from an older build means a new removal build (D12: every removal produces a named build) that reverts that item, and the items that depend on it, on top of the current build. Options: removal builds only (recommended, no per-component switches), or per-component switches for selected default-on items such as OAW-12
system_decisions: One D12 build per batch, named '<release>+build.N.<short content hash>', with a human label naming the batch, its items and each default-on behaviour change; each build lists its components with an evidence level per line (measured / static-measured / not measured), and a line with no measured evidence says 'not measured', never 'enhanced'.

Builds: 1, 2, 3, 4a (OAW-15, OAW-17, OAW-18: new flags and messages), 4b (OAW-19: exit codes, kept apart because its release target may differ), 5, 6, 7, 8 and 9; OAW-16 gets its own build only if its A/B passes (revision 3: it is a hold).
Each item lands as its own revertible commit set with its dependents named (for example OAW-13 and OAW-14 come out before OAW-12, OAW-18 before OAW-15), so a removal build can take out one item.

Records written forward stay in the project, because restoring switches only the OAW-installed layer (D12): 'files:' lines (OAW-18), 'Supersedes:' lines (OAW-20) and renderer_version frontmatter (OAW-23). Each such item states and tests how the previous build treats them (planned: read as plain text, or as an ordinary scalar by _parse_frontmatter, wiki_sync.py:31-74; not yet tested).
The restore point of each build is the previous build; a restore or removal build switches only the OAW-installed layer, never project records, then runs doctor (D12).
items.notes: Revision 3: revision 2's 'a restore removes as little as possible' and 'the other items are additive or credential refusals' were wrong (goldfish-1 #13; goldfish-2 B07, B08). Revision 2's build 4b (OAW-16, OAW-17) no longer exists: OAW-16 is a hold and OAW-17 moved to 4a.
